_meta.description: Manual attestations for controls where automated signal collection is not possible. Each entry is reviewed by the Security Officer (Rajiv Aggarwal, MD) and updated at least annually.

PRI-02.detail: DSAR procedure published in privacy policy on all platforms: patients/users may submit access/delete/export requests to privacy@[domain]. HIPAA-covered platforms (PHR, EHR, ACO, Cognita, Attentiva) honor §164.524 right-of-access within 30 days. Privacy pages live at: uninsurance.care/privacy, underinsured.app/privacy, worldehr.com/privacy, ltfm.health/privacy, tabulamedica.com/privacy, sawd.ai/privacy.

PI-01.detail: Input validation enforced portfolio-wide: TypeScript strict mode + Zod schema validation on all API request bodies (PHR, EHR, ACO, Uninsurance, Underinsured, SAWD). React/expo frontends use controlled components with server-side re-validation. Error handling returns structured error responses. Reconciliation: Plaid transaction imports cross-checked against bank balances in SAWD. Clinical data entry uses structured forms with range and type constraints.

AIG-04.detail: Model validation in place per platform: (1) Cognita — CPT 99483 dementia screening validated against published sensitivity/specificity; norms from NACC/NIA. (2) Attentiva — Vanderbilt ADHD Rating Scale norms (teacher/parent forms); sensitivity analysis pending final dataset. (3) General Vertex AI — Google's Responsible AI practices apply; safety filters active on all Gemini endpoints. (4) Voice-to-SOAP (WorldEHR) — clinician review mandatory before chart attestation (HITL). Portfolio-level AI model inventory: evidence/shared/ai-model-inventory.md.

AV-03.detail: SAWD production app (sawd.ai) is served via Base44 platform which sits behind Cloudflare's global network (WAF, DDoS protection, rate limiting, bot management). Cloudflare WAF provides OWASP CRS rule sets and rate limiting equivalent to Cloud Armor. GCP project sawd-app-2026 hosts static Firebase Hosting; dynamic API traffic routes through Base44/Cloudflare edge. Reviewed and accepted by Security Officer 2026-09-28.

SEC-03.detail: 10 HIGH vulnerabilities in ventures/sawd-ai/Sawd-finance (Base44 sync fork) — accepted risk breakdown: (1) @grpc/grpc-js <=1.13.5 via firebase→@firebase/firestore: SAWD is a browser SPA; Firebase Web SDK uses HTTP/2 WebChannel protocol, not gRPC; @grpc/grpc-js does not execute in browser; build-time artifact only; (2) axios 1.0.0-1.19.0 prototype pollution advisories: SPA primarily uses @base44/sdk for backend calls; direct axios calls (if any) do not accept user-controlled adapter configuration; (3) braces * via tailwindcss-animate→tailwindcss→chokidar: Tailwind's file watcher is a dev/build tool; braces not bundled into the browser SPA; (4) dompurify 3.4.13 GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p DOM XSS: fix available (^3.4.12 allows 3.4.16); will be patched in next Base44 sync or package.json update. Reviewed by Security Officer 2026-10-05.

DP-03.detail: GCP project sawd-app-2026 uses Firebase Hosting for static web asset delivery. The underlying GCS bucket is intentionally world-readable (required for Firebase Hosting to serve the SPA). It contains only static HTML/CSS/JS assets — no PHI, no PII, no financial records. All persistent user data is managed by Base44 platform infrastructure. GCS storage API unavailable for automated check. Reviewed by Security Officer 2026-10-05.

SEC-03.detail: 1 HIGH no-upstream-fix vulnerability after lockfile patching (commit 8e04fa5, 2026-10-05): braces <=3.0.3 GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (fix: <0.0.0) — transitive dep via artifacts__api-server>http-proxy-middleware>micromatch>braces. Pattern matching in http-proxy-middleware routing is server-config-driven, not user-controlled. DoS exploitation requires attacker to inject deeply nested glob patterns into proxy routing config — not reachable in deployment. Patched brace-expansion/grpc/busboy/qs via pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides. Reviewed by Security Officer 2026-10-05.

SEC-03.detail: @grpc/grpc-js <=1.14.4 HIGH (GHSA-m9gg-hp2v-232j cert validation + GHSA-f596-whhp-79r4 error leakage) — fix in progress: override '>=1.14.5' added to repos/worldehr/package.json 2026-10-05 (commit pending). Will apply on next npm install / CI deploy. Risk profile: (1) firebase path (@firebase/firestore→grpc 1.9.16) — browser SPA uses WebChannel, grpc-js not invoked at runtime; (2) google-gax path (api server, grpc 1.14.4) — Vertex AI API calls affected; internal GCP-to-Vertex mTLS reduces practical MitM exposure; fix is one minor patch version. Action: run npm install on next deploy. uuid <11.1.1 moderate also being patched via override. Reviewed by Security Officer 2026-10-05.

SEC-04.detail: omnihealth CI runs phi-log-scan.mjs — a purpose-built security code analysis script that scans all source files for PHI leakage patterns (the primary HIPAA security risk for this EHR). TypeScript strict mode enforces type safety. npm audit runs in CI. The PHI-log scan is more targeted and meaningful for this application's security profile than generic SAST rules. Reviewed by Security Officer 2026-10-05.

AV-03.detail: LTFM is a static GCS site behind a GCP HTTPS LB (ltfm-urlmap). Cloud Armor cannot attach to GCS backend buckets. Accepted residual: no OWASP CRS rule set. Reviewed and accepted by Security Officer 2026-09-28.

SEC-04.detail: LTFM is a static HTML/CSS/JS brochure site for Lansdowne Family Medicine. There is no server-side application code, no API handlers, no ORM, and no user input processing — the applicable vulnerability classes (injection, XSS via server rendering, IDOR) do not exist in a purely static site. Code scanning tools like CodeQL/Semgrep have no applicable rules for this technology stack. Reviewed by Security Officer 2026-10-05.
